newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet says board will meet May 23.
newsitem.headline: Eramet says board will meet May 23.

text.p: French mining group Eramet said on Tuesday that its board will meet on May 23 to review a number of requests put forward by staff representatives and shareholders.
"There will be a board meeting on May 23. Its aim is to review all resolutions and demands that have were submitted," a company spokesman told Reuters.
Asked if the board will also set a new date for the annual general meeting, the spokesman said "I don't know. The board will meet to review the events of the last two weeks,"
Last week Eramet postponed an annual shareholders' meeting set for May 29 to give itself more time to consider the requests.
Eramet is caught in a battle of nerves with its main shareholder, the French state, over the distribution of mining assets in New Caledonia.

State holding Erap, which has a 55 percent stake in Eramet, has threatened to take control of Eramet's board and to replace chairman Yves Rambaud, who opposes any plans to curb the group's development in the South Pacific Island.
Institutional investors, concerned over the way the state has handled the mining dispute, have put forward proposals aimed at insuring the future independence of Eramet's board.
Staff representatives want employees to be given the chance to select three directors under a 1983 public sector law.

Eramet is under pressure from the government to swap mining titles with a local mining company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to help supply a nickel smelter SMSP and Canadian group Falconbridge plan to build in the north of the territory.
The exchange is seen as a political gesture to appease Kanak nationalists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence.
The legal experts and SMSP and Eramet met last week to discuss the terms of the planned asset swap and further meetings are scheduled in coming weeks, the spokesman said.
"Progress is being made. Meetings are taking place," he said but he did not provide further details.
One of the main issues to settle is the amount and the terms of the financial compensation that must be paid to Eramet to exchange its Koniambo field for SMSP's Poum field.
